learning_objective: 🎯 Uncover the invisible pushes and pulls that rule our universe! Master Newton's Three Laws of Motion and understand concepts like inertia, friction, and momentum.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: If you and a friend push a box from opposite sides with the exact same strength, the forces are Balanced, and the box won't move. Motion only changes when an Unbalanced force is applied!

An object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and direction UNLESS acted upon by an unbalanced force. Mass is the measure of inertia; heavier things are harder to move or stop.

The rate of change of momentum of an object is proportional to the applied unbalanced force. Simply put: Force equals Mass times Acceleration ($F = ma$). To accelerate a heavy truck, you need a much bigger force than to accelerate a bicycle!

For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. When you jump off a small boat, you push the boat backward (action), and the boat pushes you forward (reaction). They act on two DIFFERENT objects.
Momentum ($p = mv$) is the 'quantity of motion'. In a closed system with no external forces, the total momentum before a collision is exactly equal to the total momentum after the collision.

fun_activity.title: 🪙 The Coin & Card Trick (Inertia)
fun_activity.instructions: Place a smooth playing card over the mouth of a glass. Put a heavy coin in the center of the card. Flick the card hard horizontally with your finger. The card flies away, but the coin drops straight into the glass! The coin's 'Inertia of Rest' kept it in place.

exam_tips: 📌 Real-life examples of Newton's Laws are highly tested. E.g., A passenger falling backward when a bus starts suddenly is First Law (Inertia). A rocket taking off is Third Law.
📌 Always write the unit of Force as Newton (N), where $1 N = 1 kg \cdot m/s^2$.
📌 Be prepared to solve numericals using the Conservation of Momentum formula: $m_1 u_1 + m_2 u_2 = m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2$.
quick_recap: ⭐ Friction is a force that always acts in the opposite direction to the intended motion.
⭐ The mathematical formulation of the Second Law ($F=ma$) shows that acceleration is inversely proportional to mass.
⭐ Catching a fast cricket ball by pulling your hands backward reduces the rate of change of momentum, preventing injury (Second Law).
